text: Brown spot disease (ចំនួអុចត្នួត, "chomngu uch tnaot" - sesame-seed-like spot) is caused by the fungus Helminthosporium oryzae (also classified as Bipolaris oryzae). The source describes small oval brown-to-dark-brown spots, resembling sesame seeds, that appear first on the leaves and later on the grain hull itself - which lowers milling and market quality even in cases where the yield loss looks mild. Notably, the source links this disease specifically to fields that are short on nitrogen and to fields where standing water has run low - i.e. plants under nutrient or water stress are the most vulnerable, which fits the general pattern that brown spot is a stress-associated fungus rather than one that needs heavy rain or a dense canopy the way blast or sheath blight do. Management: correct nitrogen shortfalls through balanced, properly-timed fertilization (see the SSNM entries in this knowledge base); avoid letting fields dry out for extended stretches during vulnerable growth stages; use clean, healthy seed since the fungus can carry over on seed as well as on infected straw; and remove infected residue after harvest instead of leaving it in the field.
